gap_text: The SDK receipt lane has no automatic spool expiry and no loss/recovery acceptance under a full disk or an extended outage (observability/receipt.json line 258).
next_check: Point the SDK receipt spool at a size-limited tmpfs, fill it, stop the collector for an extended interval, then restore both and count lost versus replayed receipts. Add and test an expiry policy.

arms.arm: point the SDK receipt spool at a size-limited tmpfs and fill it
arms.detail: 128 KiB tmpfs in an unprivileged user+mount namespace; unchanged write_observation()

arms.arm: stop the collector for an extended interval
arms.detail: 180.0 s; plus a Loki-only outage of about 335 s and an overlapping collector+Loki outage

arms.arm: restore both and count lost versus replayed receipts
arms.detail: counted by observation_id in Loki and in the collector file/events receipt

arms.arm: add and test an expiry policy
arms.detail: spool_expiry.py, 6 unit tests, live run on the tmpfs spool

preregistration.expectation: Inside an unprivileged user+mount namespace, a size-limited tmpfs spool (e.g. 256 KiB) will fill; the SDK receipt writer will fail atomically on ENOSPC without partial files; with the collector stopped for an extended interval and later restarted, file_log will replay every complete receipt into an isolated Loki with no duplicates; an added expiry policy script will delete only receipts older than the TTL whose ingestion is confirmed.
preregistration.criteria: Count: receipts attempted, receipts written, ENOSPC refusals, partial files (must be 0), receipts in Loki after restore (must equal written, distinct receipt_id), duplicates (must be 0). Expiry policy test: unit tests plus a run on the tmpfs spool that frees space and allows new writes. Extended interval = at least 3 minutes collector down and Loki down for part of it.

followup.label: follow-up preregistration, written after the first gap-4 run (raw/4-spool-outage.json) and before the follow-up runs
followup.expectation: (a) Space freed by the expiry policy is released only after the collector file receiver closes its handles on deleted files, so writes fail for a short interval after expiry and then succeed. (b) With otlphttp/loki retry_on_failure.max_elapsed_time set to 0s (retry indefinitely, persistent queue already configured), a 330 s Loki outage loses 0 of 8 receipts; the unchanged configuration loses them (as in the first run).
followup.criteria: (a) Record deleted-but-open file descriptors held by otelcol right after expiry (count of /proc/<pid>/fd links ending in '(deleted)'), time until statvfs free bytes > 0, and whether a write succeeds after that. (b) Run the Loki-outage phase with the overlay; pass = 8/8 in Loki after restore, no duplicates. Both variants use the same isolated harness.

fix_round.label: fix-round preregistration (after the independent Codex review in raw/review-codex-round1.txt), written before the fix-round runs
fix_round.expectation: Overlapping outage with the unchanged configuration: collector down 0-180 s, Loki down 60-240 s; receipts written during the collector outage are replayed at 180 s into the persistent queue and delivered after Loki returns (within the 300 s retry window), so 0 are lost and none duplicated.
fix_round.criteria: lost_in_loki == 0 and duplicates == {} for receipts written while the collector was down.
fix_round.committed_in: the commit 'Record the Codex review and preregister the fix round' (2026-09-23T03:28:46Z, before the fix-round runs)

note: Measured on a size-limited tmpfs spool with the unchanged write_observation() helper. A full disk refuses new receipts atomically (ENOSPC, no partial or pending files). A 180 s collector outage replayed all 32 receipts with no loss or duplicates, and an overlapping collector+Loki outage within the retry window lost 0. A Loki outage longer than the exporter retry window (about 335 s) dropped every receipt sent in it (8/8, reproduced twice) from Loki; they stayed in the spool and file/events receipt, and file_log does not re-read them. Setting otlphttp/loki retry_on_failure.max_elapsed_time to 0s lost 0/8 in the same test. A Loki-confirmed-only expiry policy (spool_expiry.py, 6 unit tests) frees space once the file receiver closes its handles on the deleted files. Remaining: apply the max_elapsed_time change to observability/collector/collector.yaml (outside this unit's paths) and schedule spool_expiry.py so expiry is automatic; collector queue-directory exhaustion and multi-hour outages were not tested.
limits: Isolated collector + Loki in an unprivileged user/mount namespace; not the live spool or services.
"Extended" here means 180 s (collector), about 335 s (Loki) and an overlapping window of 261.5 s; multi-hour outages and a full collector queue directory were not exercised.
Loss is counted in Loki by observation_id; the collector file/events receipt had every record throughout.
The expiry policy is a script plus tests; it is not wired into any timer or unit.
